name: ULA Vulcan VC6L (2x BE-4, 6x GEM 63XL, LEO-optimized Centaur V / CV-L with 2x RL10C-1-1A, 21.3 m fairing) — TIMELINE mode

diameter_m.derived: 63.7 in motor diameter, Northrop Grumman Propulsion Products Catalog p.39 (https://cdn.northropgrumman.com/-/media/wp-content/uploads/NG-Propulsion-Products-Catalog.pdf

propellant_kg.derived: 105,497 lbm propellant (NG catalog p.39, 73°F vacuum performance table) × 0.45359237

thrust_vac_N.derived: total-time-average thrust 334,063 lbf vacuum at 73°F (NG catalog p.39) × 4.448221615

thrust_sl_N.assumption: catalog quotes vacuum average only; used as the constant average for the whole 87.3 s burn (grain throttle unpublished). Sea-level loss at liftoff not modelled.

isp_vac_s.note: GEM 63XL specific impulse 280.3 lbf-s/lbm, vacuum, 73°F, p.39

ignition_s.note: UG §2.1: SRBs ignite after BE-4 health check and the vehicle lifts off; sim T-0 is liftoff with SRBs and BE-4 already running

cutoff_s.note: GEM 63XL burn time 87.3 s (catalog summary table and p.39)

separation_s.note: UG §2.1: 'The SRBs are jettisoned after burnout is detected. This occurs roughly 100 seconds into flight.' Approximate UG typical, not this flight.

propellant_kg.assumption: ULA UG §1.4: tanks 'hold over a million pounds' of LOX and LNG (>453,592 kg). 460 t is a floor-plus-margin so a 292 s full-thrust BECO (UG Fig. 2.1.1-2, CCSFS example) at the derived mdot leaves a small PU residual. Exact load and the UG throttle to 4.6 g are unpublished.

dry_kg.assumption: Secondary: Reich, Raketen: Die Internationale Enzyklopädie (2020) via Wikipedia 'Vulcan Centaur' (empty mass 28,600 kg). Not a ULA primary figure.

thrust_sl_N.derived: 2 × 2,446.5 kN (550k-lbf) sea-level (ULA UG Table 1.4-1 and Vulcan Leo 1 mission page)

thrust_vac_N.derived: 2 × 2,446.5 kN × (340/320); mdot held at the sea-level pair F_sl/(Isp_sl g0). Isp pair is secondary (see isp_vac_s).

isp_vac_s.assumption: Vacuum Isp 340 s from Jeff Bezos / Tim Dodd factory tour (15 Aug 2024) as cited on Wikipedia 'Vulcan Centaur'/'BE-4'; ULA does not publish BE-4 Isp. Sea-level 320 s from Reich 2020 (same Wikipedia citation) used only to derive vac thrust.

ignition_s.note: UG §2.1: booster phase begins with ignition of the two BE-4 engines

cutoff_s.note: UG Fig. 2.1.1-2 (two-burn 1800 m/s GTO, CCSFS, 'Approximate Times & Values') BECO T+00:04:52. TYPICAL east-coast example, not this flight. (Fig. 2.1.1-1 VSFB SSO is 286 s; Cert-1 webcast 299 s on a 2-SRB vehicle.)

separation_s.note: UG Fig. 2.1.1-2 booster/Centaur separation T+00:04:58 (typical CCSFS example)

diameter_m.note: Centaur LEO 17.7 ft (5.4 m) diameter, 35 ft (10.7 m) length

propellant_kg.derived: ULA fact sheet / Centaur V '120,000-lb propellant capacity' for the high-energy variant (https://www.ulalaunch.com/docs/default-source/rockets/vulcancentaur.pdf = 54,431 kg; ULA blog 2 Jun 2026: the LEO-optimized Centaur V 'carries a third less propellant than the high energy variant' (https://blog.ulalaunch.com/blog/vulcan-new-centaur-v-version-readies-for-amazon-leo → 54,431 × 2/3 = 36,287 kg

dry_kg.assumption: CV-L dry mass unpublished. CV-HE empty mass has only secondary encyclopedia figures (~5.5 t). 4,800 kg is a labelled stand-in for the shorter (35 ft vs ~41 ft) LEO-optimized stage, which ULA says accounts for less overall weight.

thrust_sl_N.assumption: upper-stage start is in vacuum after BECO; SL rating unpublished, vac thrust used

isp_vac_s.assumption: RL10C vacuum Isp 453.8 s as listed on Wikipedia 'Vulcan Centaur' citing the L3Harris RL10 datasheet; the datasheet PDF was not retrieved this turn (vendor URL served HTML). Treat as a secondary figure.

ignition_s.note: UG Fig. 2.1.1-2 MES1 T+00:05:08, typical CCSFS example (6 s after booster/Centaur sep)

cutoff_s.assumption: LV-01 MES1 duration unpublished. 600 s MES1 (T+908 s) is a starting value in the UG-typical 11–12 min first-burn band (Fig. 2.1.1-1/2), to be tuned so MES1 inserts a ~180 × 450 km transfer (apogee = Amazon's published 450 km KA-01 insertion; perigee 180 km ASSUMED). MES2 is modelled post-cutoff at first apoapsis.

mass_kg.assumption: 21.3 m (70 ft) long 5.4 m composite PLF mass unpublished by ULA/Beyond Gravity; 2,500 kg is a labelled stand-in (order of a large composite fairing), NOT a measurement.

jettison_time_s.note: UG Fig. 2.1.1-2 PLF jettison T+00:05:16 during MES1 (typical CCSFS example). UG §2.1: jettisoned during the first Centaur burn after the heating constraint is satisfied.

cd.assumption: not published; generic slender-launcher Cd (same as Electron/F9). Not fitted.

payload_kg.basis: 40 Amazon Leo satellites, mass unpublished (Amazon says production sats weigh more than 1,000 lb / 450 kg → 18 t floor before dispenser). Upper bound = UG/fact-sheet VC6 LEO PSW 27,200 kg (200 km / 28.7°). Fitted payload is NOT an estimate of the real stack.

header_notes: Vulcan VC6L: 6 GEM 63XL (NG catalog p.39 masses, 87.3 s burn, 334,063 lbf vacuum time-average thrust, Isp 280.3 s), 2×BE-4 550k-lbf SL (ULA UG / Vulcan Leo 1 page), LEO-optimized Centaur V (ULA: 35 ft, a third less propellant than the 120,000-lb CV-HE, twin RL10C-1-1A at 23,825 lbf each), 21.3 m fairing (ULA).

TIMELINE mode: booster/Centaur event times from ULA UG Fig. 2.1.1-2 (CCSFS two-burn example, 'Approximate Times & Values') plus NG 87.3 s SRB burn and UG '~100 s' SRB jettison — TYPICAL sequence, not LV-01's unpublished timeline. MES1 cutoff is an ASSUMED duration, tuned so the first burn targets a 180 × 450 km transfer.

BE-4 Isp, booster dry mass, CV-L dry mass and fairing mass are secondary or ASSUMED (see fields). BE-4 throttle to 4.6 g (UG) is not modelled; full published sea-level/derived-vac thrust is used throughout the booster phase.
